## 席位核对 · ACCEPT

## 维护者速读（席位校正）

The body's lines stand as written, read against the diff. One consequence is the ruling's own and is named in the 风险 line and the changeset: a reader holding only the ledger's read grant, who cannot read the settings store, no longer sees NEW `config_change` rows. `view_all_audit_log` holders (admins by default) see every row; older null-`record_id` rows are unchanged. Nothing becomes visible that was not before. Veto at this PR if that narrowing is not wanted.

## 席位核对

- **Shape:** read the diff myself (22 files, +1123 / −78). `upsertRow` returns `rowId` (probed row on update, insert result on insert, null for the in-memory store); the sink records it as `record_id` beside the unchanged `object_name`; `metadata` and the `new_value` digest are unchanged. `sys_audit_log_detail` lists ledger rows keyed `record_id` ↔ `record_id`, newest first, no "New" (ledger is get/list only). `sys_queue_detail` lists `sys_queue_member` keyed `queue` ↔ `name` via the published `relationshipValueField` (`component.zod.ts`), so the member column and ADR-0142's name key are untouched. Both pages are `kind: 'full'`, `isDefault`, labels in each plugin's shipped locales.
- **Read gate:** `audit-log-read-visibility.ts` only moves `config_change` from the "about no record" class to the record-gate class in its header; the gate's code path already judges any row with a `record_id`, so the new rows ride the existing gate and the field redaction, as the CRUD mirror's rows about the same write already do.
- **Narrowing question (report 6672470118):** `Clause-②: no`, no (narrowing) arm. The narrowing is runtime read visibility of ledger rows under an existing gate, not a change to a published contract's acceptance set: no schema, key, status or accepted input changes. It is disclosed in the changeset and 速读 above instead.
- **Declarations:** `Refs #30209` (rows 1–3, 5 stay open on the card), `Clause-②: no`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, patch changeset on the three packages; consistent with the diff.
- **Out of scope / follow-up:** the console's Audit Logs drawer does not link to the new record page; the seat files a ui card at landing.
- **Landing:** `check-governed-merges --pr 30728`: NOT governed, 1201 changed lines (≤ 3000). CI on this head is still running; the seat lands with `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable` once it is green or expected-skip.

### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, `@objectstack/plugin-sharing`, `@objectstack/service-settings`, touching **39** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-log-read-visibility.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**58** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ab44ec94b0362bafdf5f610b1d121655cd39a5fa`.

⛔ **15** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-log-read-visibility.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `created_at (literal, 43 pages)`
- **4** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **221** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **22** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ab44ec94b0362bafdf5f610b1d121655cd39a5fa` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a1f4c72d067f7886d24ae81d1b912f94eb87d4ba` — the merge of head `f6c2de448e069709b45b53d3b75055dd2df805a3` into base `ab44ec94b0362bafdf5f610b1d121655cd39a5fa`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a1f4c72d067f7886d24ae81d1b912f94eb87d4ba && git checkout a1f4c72d067f7886d24ae81d1b912f94eb87d4ba
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ab44ec94b0362bafdf5f610b1d121655cd39a5fa f6c2de448e069709b45b53d3b75055dd2df805a3 && git checkout -B drift-repro ab44ec94b0362bafdf5f610b1d121655cd39a5fa && git merge --no-ff f6c2de448e069709b45b53d3b75055dd2df805a3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ab44ec94b0362bafdf5f610b1d121655cd39a5fa
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ab44ec94b0362bafdf5f610b1d121655cd39a5fa` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.
